title: Finite-field factorization and sparse-polynomial root testing
exact_target: For a degree-$n$ polynomial over $\mathbb F_q$, is factorization possible deterministically in time polynomial in $n$ and $\log q$? Determine the unconditional complexity of factoring $x^2-a$, and the optimal exponent in randomized factorization over $\mathbb F_2$. For a collection of polynomials of degree two or three, is deciding whether all split into linear factors faster through their product or through separate tests? Finally, can one decide whether $x^\alpha+ax^\beta+b$ has a root in $\mathbb F_q$ in time polynomial in $\log q$, where $0<\beta<\alpha\leq q-1$ and $a,b\in\mathbb F_q$?
